recipes.name: Mushrooms Berkeley
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Combine brown sugar, red wine, Dijon mustard, and Worcestershire sauce in a bowl until sugar completely dissolved; set aside.

Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add onion; cook and stir until translucent, 5 to 7 minutes. Add mushrooms; season with black pepper. Cook and stir until mushrooms reduce in size and begin to brown, about 3 minutes ; stir in wine mixture. Simmer until hot, 1 to 2 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Mushrooms Berkeley
raw_recipe.description: This mushrooms Berkeley recipe combines sautéed mushrooms and sweet onions in a red wine sauce make a nice topping for pork loin or your favorite dish.

review.reviewBody:
I would leave out the sugar. Was good with it, but I think it would be better without. Very nice way to serve mushrooms. I used a Malbec wine and served it with a pot roast I cooked in the pressure cooker (no gravy).

Edit: I tried it again without the sugar and it was much better. Next time I am going to try white wine which will make a nicer looking sauce - the red wine and the mustard make it muddy looking.

These mushrooms are great made like this. Two tips: if you'd like them more tangy leave out the brown sugar. Put half a teaspoon in for a balanced taste. To have them on the sweeter side, feel free to add more of the brown sugar. It is up to you and it's a matter of taste. To mine I add a teaspoon or less of the sugar and they have always been a hit. Then if you'd like to have your mushrooms softer, wait and add the sauce after they have become browner. If you'd like them firmer at the end, then add the sauce as they begin to brown but are still somewhat firm. Normally, I continue to cook them in the skillet over medium heat for another 10mins after adding the sauce. They are great as a side to chicken or pork.

So delicious! I didn’t even use all of the butter that the recipe called for and it was still super yummy. I used only about 1/4 cup of butter: using half of which in the beginning with a generous drizzle of safflower oil and then added the other half after the mushrooms shrunk down a bit. A+!

A great change from everyday mushrooms and onions. The only change I made was to use 2 tbsp. of maple syrup instead of brown sugar with Merlot for the wine. I used the sauce to de-glaze the pan and added the mushroom mixture back into it after the sauce had reduced a bit. Served them over grilled pork chops.

The original recipe is definitely 5 star. It calls for 1/2 bell pepper (green) cut in 1 inch chunks in addition to the onions (regular yellow is fine) and mushrooms. Also, the cooking time after adding the sauce is more like 45 minutes. It cooks down to a lovely thick state, "nasty looking" according to the original, but absolutely wonderful on toasts at a party. Try using tamari as a sub for Worcestershire (as my friend who gave me this years ago advised.)

You know when you like a recipe but dont have any of the ingredients but you know that what you have will work. Yeah, well, I did that. Was still delish!! 
I used tamari sauce and a honey garlic sauce w a spot of mustard in it. and cooked it all down. Have used it on top of potatoes, pasta, eggs, meat. Will make again with anything!

I meant to add that I usually triple the vegetables but only double the sauce to make more. I cook over high heat until the sauce starts to thicken and then slowly decrease the heat and stir more frequently to keep it from sticking. I find it takes a good long time for the thickening to start.

A strong flavor reminiscent of BBQ sauce. Tasted good if that's the taste you're going for. I thought it was going to be a lighter wine sauce flavor, was not. Only used 2 TBPS of brown sugar and would recommend. Used King Trumpet Mushrooms and cut in 4ths. I would recommend cutting in 8ths next time because they did become chewy. Would make for a BBQ side dish because it was very moist and would compliment charcoal flavor.
A keeper, delicious! I used 1 tbs. of brown sugar per other suggestions. I used sherry cooking wine and whole grain mustard. Served with a roast.

Wonderful; thank you. The only wine I have in the house is Marsala, so that's what I used. I simmered it all a few minutes until the sauce thickened up a bit. We put it over steak & my husband said it was better than a restaurant. Then we used the leftovers for mushroom swiss burgers. Tell me a burger joint that puts Marsala wine in their mushroom sauce, ha!

This recipe is excellent. It is a keeper. I unfortunately had to use Sherry as I had no red wine. However, the outcome was spectacular. I put it as a side for the Breaded Pork Chops posted in this website....EXCELLENT combination! I followed the recommendations of others who suggest to forgo the sugar. I do agree this recipe without it is perfect. Personally, I do not like to add sugar to plates that are not desserts or sweets. I am definitely doing this again. Now, at the moment I had to reduce the recipe for 2 people and noticed that there was a bit of extra sauce which my hubby wipped off from the plate with some crusty bread....
I have used this recipe for over a year now. Love it!
Excellent recipe. Used less butter.
I really liked it....will make it again
Love it, use half sugar and half butter
I made this and put it over baked pork chops. It paired well together but was a bit too sweet for our taste. If I make it again, I will use less sugar.
Hmmmmmm good! This is straightforward and well paired with beef, pork or fish.
Little less sugar would have made it much better. I added a little zucchini.
Delicious and easy. Omitted the sugar and didn’t miss it all

It is probably because I used a very honey mustard (Woeber's much more honey than most!) instead of the Dijon and half of the brown sugar, but my 'sauce' turns into well browned glazed mushrooms with a lot of greasy liquid that I just left in the pan...but the mushrooms sure were tasty with the pot roast! I was cooking the mushrooms separate without onions to cater to some conflicting taste preferences. Since I made a significant substitution, I can't really rate the original, but I thought there might be someone else with honey mustard who might need to know you don't have to throw it all away when the sauce breaks.
